chunks: What was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Faḍālah, from Abān, from Muslim, from Abī Ḥafṣ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say:

A nosebleed, blood, and vomiting do not invalidate the salat (prayer). So whoever experiences discomfort should take the hand of a man from the people in the row and bring him forward—that is, if he is an Imam.

key_terms.أَذًى: harm or discomfort experienced during prayer
key_terms.إِمَامًا: the prayer leader in congregational salat
key_terms.الدَّمُ: blood, mentioned as not invalidating the prayer here
key_terms.الصَّفِّ: the row of worshippers in congregational prayer
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the salat (prayer) being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْقَيْءُ: vomiting, mentioned as not invalidating the prayer here

ai.seo_question: Does a nosebleed, bleeding, or vomiting invalidate the salat (prayer), and what should an Imam do if it happens during congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a nosebleed, bleeding, or vomiting does not invalidate the salat (prayer). If the one affected is leading the congregation, he should appoint another man from the row to step forward and continue as Imam.
